name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (battle drop-collection helper). Name accurately reflects behavior: collects 3-byte drop entries from characters that are pending death (wHP_current==0 but bFlags CHARFLAG_DEAD not yet set). No Ghidra address residue; no domain ID to preserve.
purpose: Scan the runtime character array and pack into out_buffer the 3-byte drop entry of every party member that has just taken a fatal hit (HP==0, not yet flagged dead) and whose drop slot is non-empty (type != 0xFF), returning the number of entries collected.
logic_summary: drop_count=0; for i in 0..data_fd2_battle_party_member_count: take pChar = runtime_char_array[i]; if (pChar.bFlags & CHARFLAG_DEAD)==0 AND pChar combat_aux[10] (flat offset 0x31) != 0xFF AND pChar.wHP_current (offset 0x40)==0 then memmove(out_buffer + drop_count*3, &pChar combat_aux[10], 3); drop_count++. Return drop_count. Differs from sibling fd2_collect_dead_char_drops only in the slot predicate: this one accepts any type != 0xFF (item/gold/battle_event/scripted_dialog), the sibling accepts only type==3 (scripted_dialog). Shares the same loop shape; in the binary the epilogue is borrowed (tail JMP to 0x1B64D) but that is an asm-level detail with no source effect.

params.name: out_buffer
params.semantics: Address (cast to uint32 by callers) of a caller-local byte buffer that receives the packed 3-byte drop entries (entry = byte type + uint16 value). Callers pass a stack buffer (drops_buf / drops_buffer) and feed the returned count plus this same buffer into fd2_process_battle_drop_entries.
params.reason: Descriptive of its role as the output buffer; no address residue, not a generic param_N placeholder.

returns.semantics: Number of 3-byte drop entries written into out_buffer (count of pending-death characters with a non-empty drop slot).

notes: Existing src comment (btl_turn.c:371-376) is correct and concise; it defines behavior by delta against the sibling fd2_collect_dead_char_drops whose full predicate is documented at btl_turn.c:345-348 -- kept as-is. Ghidra plate is much more detailed but fully consistent with src and decompilation (no contradiction / not stale / not blank), so plate left untouched. Decompiler shows the field as pCombat_aux_block[10]; src uses the equivalent flat byte offset pChar[0x31] (combat_aux block base 0x27 + 10). All 4 callers (fd2_apply_use_effect_dispatch, fd2_execute_ai_physical_attack, fd2_player_inline_action_menu_dispatch, fd2_spell_selection_menu_main) pass a local drops buffer and use the return as the entry count. No logic concerns.
